title: Lifting generators modulo $IN$ to the graded pieces $I^nN/I^{n+1}N$
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, and $f:M\to N$ a homomorphism of $R$-modules. For an $R$-module $P$ and $n\ge0$ write $I^nP$ for the submodule of $P$ generated by the products $ap$ with $a\in I^n$, $p\in P$ (so $I^0P=P$). Assume that $N=f(M)+IN$, i.e. the composite $M\to N\to N/IN$ is surjective. Then for every $n\ge0$ and every $y\in I^nN$ there is $x\in I^nM$ with $f(x)-y\in I^{n+1}N$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087Z (lemma-finite-over-rees-algebra), proof (lines 6621-6630): the assertion that $\bigoplus I^nM/I^{n+1}M$ is 'clearly' finite over $\bigoplus I^n/I^{n+1}$; this node is the module-theoretic fact behind 'clearly'.
